answers.core: Thor is already included in the engine. The page that the Godot documentation links to to show what part of the spec is supported ([Support is limited](https://www.thorvg.org/about#:~:text=among%20the%20svg%20tiny%20specs%2C%20yet%20unsupported%20features%20in%20the%20thorvg%20are%20the%20following)) explicitly mentions SVG-filters, so many godot-users will get the impression that these are already available.
answers.workaround: Obviously all these filters can be implemented in a dozen different ways: You can use shaders to blur stuff, or copy your assets to create faux drop-shadows. But this is pretty cumbersome, what makes SVG's great is that they can be very expressive: you need only a few lines to create very complex images.

title: Allow for SVG-filter functionality (drop-shadow, gaussian blur) by exposing ThorVG scene-effects .
